- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward by 2–5% in next 3–7 days.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) after a peak, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 3–7 days ahead.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.33), model tends to overfit recent trends; apply smoothing or reduce forecast volatility by 1–2% for next 10 days.  
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward bias correction of 1–3% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the window; reduce first 5–7 days’ forecast by 1–2% to align with true mean reversion.
